Authors: Zhou Y, Chen S, Zhang Y, Jiang Y, Xiao M, Xin X, Shi Z, Zhang L
Journal: Cancer | DOI: 10.1002/cncr.70648
Published: 2026-Dec-01
PMID: 43069728



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is central to cervical lesion development, but single viral-load measurements may not capture heterogeneous viral dynamics. This study characterized longitudinal viral-load trajectories among women with persistent infection and evaluated their associations with cervical lesions and incremental predictive value beyond baseline factors. METHODS: In this prospective cohort of 1502 HPV-positive women followed at approximately 6-month intervals, latent class growth analysis using actual follow-up time was conducted among 624 women with type-specific persistent infection. Associations between trajectory group and any cervical lesion (low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion or high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion [HSIL]) were assessed using multivariable logistic regression; HSIL was explored using Firth-penalized regression. Discrimination, calibration, and decision-curve analysis were used to assess incremental predictive performance. RESULTS: Of 1170 women with classifiable outcomes, 624 had persistent infection. Four trajectories were identified: low stable (39.6%), moderate declining (18.9%), moderate increasing (29.8%), and persistently high (11.7%). Any-lesion prevalence was 10.9%, 17.8%, 74.2%, and 90.4%, respectively (p < .001). Compared with the low-stable group, fully adjusted odds ratios (ORs) were 1.95 (95% CI, 1.02-3.74), 29.66 (95% CI, 16.75-52.51), and 124.29 (95% CI, 47.30-326.60) for the other groups, respectively. The persistently high group was also associated with HSIL (OR, 9.47; 95% CI, 3.18-33.09). The optimism-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) increased from 0.713 for the base model to 0.888 for both the simple longitudinal and trajectory models and 0.899 for the joint model. CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal HPV viral-load dynamics identified clinically distinct risk phenotypes. Moderate-increasing and persistently high trajectories were strongly associated with cervical lesions, whereas longitudinal information improved discrimination beyond baseline measurements. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

item.title: #2 [0/100] Impact of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists on Head and Neck Cancer: Integrated Evidence From TCGA Genomic Analysis and a US Multicenter Database Study.

Authors: Chen TY, Jin L, Mao PC, Chou CW, Chen HY, Chang R, Li CJ, Liu WS
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70805
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43079591



Abstract:
Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a risk factor for head and neck cancer (HNC), but the effects of antidiabetic drugs on this risk are unclear. We evaluated glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) versus dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4is) or sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) using the TriNetX US electronic health record database, while investigating the molecular role of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP1R) in HNC. Adults ≥ 40 years with newly diagnosed T2DM (2012-2024) were studied retrospectively. Among > 250 million records, 105,605 GLP-1RA users were propensity-score matched 1:1 with 105,605 nonusers. Over a median 5-year follow-up, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly lower risks of incident HNC (HR: 0.723; 95% CI: 0.617-0.848) and all-cause mortality (HR: 0.737; 95% CI: 0.715-0.759). Results remained consistent across sex, age, obesity, smoking, alcohol use, GLP-1RA type, and further sensitivity analyses. Molecular analyses showed that higher GLP1R expression was associated with better overall survival in The Cancer Genome Atlas Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (TCGA-HNSC). GLP1R expression progressively decreased from normal to tumor and metastatic tissues, correlated with oncogenic mutation status, and was inversely associated with cell-cycle programs. In an independent multi-institutional biobank (Tri-VGH Biobank), GLP1R expression was significantly lower in tumor than matched adjacent non-tumor tissues (27 pairs), findings confirmed by tumor immunofluorescence. Overall, these epidemiological and molecular findings support a potential protective role of GLP-1RA/GLP1R signaling in HNC.

Authors: Kirke DN, Roof SA, Courey M
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70566
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43078569



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We present our experience with open total cricoid ring resection/partial laryngectomy with free flap reconstruction in the setting of cricoid chondrosarcoma. We aimed to assess whether long-term outcomes yielded appropriate oncologic and functional results to justify avoidance of total laryngectomy. METHODS: Retrospective chart review of patients undergoing open total cricoid ring resection/partial laryngectomy for low to moderate grade cricoid chondrosarcoma. All patients were reconstructed with an autologous rib, wrapped with vascularized fascia harvested from an anterolateral thigh free flap. RESULTS: Five patients (four male and one female) were identified. The median age of diagnosis was 55.2 years (range: 46-62) and average follow-up time was approximately 2.54 years (range: 37-299 weeks). No patient has required a completion laryngectomy. All five (100%) patients are tolerating an oral diet, while four (80%) have been decannulated. CONCLUSIONS: This is an oncologically safe approach and is a functionally viable alternative to total laryngectomy.

Authors: Nagarajan N, Brondfield S, Qureshi K, Villa A
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70530
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43078522



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) are an emerging and promising class of anticancer therapeutics. This retrospective study aimed to characterize the oral toxicities associated with ADC treatment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study was conducted using de-identified clinical data from the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) PatientExploreR database through 2024. A total of 13 ADCs were included in the analysis. Demographic characteristics, cancer diagnoses, treatment data, and oral toxicity data were retrieved for all eligible patients. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS: Descriptive statistics summarized demographic characteristics, smoking status, oral toxicity prevalence, and median time to onset. Associations between oral toxicity categories and sex, race, and smoking status were assessed using Pearson's chi-square or Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact tests. RESULTS: A total of 1144 patients who received ADC therapy were included in the study, including 59.7% females, 15.9% males, and 24.0% unknown. Oral toxicities were recorded in 13.7% of patients, with mucosal lesions being the most prevalent (10.5%), followed by dry mouth (2.3%) and orofacial neuropathies (1.0%). A Pearson's chi-square test demonstrated a significant association between sex at birth and oral toxicity category (p = 0.023). The frequency of oral mucosal lesions varied significantly across the ADCs (Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test with Monte Carlo simulation, 100 000 replicates; p < 0.0001). The frequency of dry mouth and orofacial neuropathies did not differ significantly among the ADCs (p = 0.412 and 0.297). CONCLUSION: Given the expanding use of ADCs in cancer therapy, characterization of their toxicity profile is essential. In this study, oral toxicities were observed in 13.7% of patients, with oral mucosal lesions being the predominant toxicity, followed by dry mouth.

Authors: Sanz-Garcia E, Spreafico A, Hosni A, de Almeida JR, McPartlin A, Eng L, Goldstein DP, Hope A, Hahn E, Yao C, et al.
Journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research | DOI: 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-26-3112
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43077433



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Molecular residual disease (MRD) interception has not been studied in locoregionally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (LA-HNSCC). MERIDIAN evaluates whether rilvegostomig, an anti-PD-1/TIGIT bispecific antibody, could clear ctDNA in MRD setting. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Patients with stage III HPV-positive or stage III-IVB HPV-negative LA-HNSCC received definitive treatment (surgery ± adjuvant therapy, radiation, or chemoradiation). ctDNA was assessed using an exome-based tumor-informed assay at baseline and surveillance. Patients with detectable ctDNA during MRD window (8-12 weeks post-definitive therapy), no progression, and PD-L1 ≥1 were eligible for randomization (3:1) to rilvegostomig or observation. Plasma HPV DNA was evaluated using HPV sequencing. RESULTS: Of 52 enrolled patients, 42 were evaluable; 57% had oropharyngeal cancer (OPC), mostly treated with chemoradiation. Six patients (14%) were ctDNA positive at the MRD window: 3 had progression, 1 had PD-L1 <1, 1 received rilvegostomig, and 1 was observed. The treated MRD-positive patient achieved ctDNA clearance at 10 weeks and remained recurrence-free through 23.4 months of follow-up. The two untreated MRD-positive patients showed substantial lead times to progression (190 and 235 days). Excluding the treated patient, ctDNA positivity at the MRD window was associated with worse RFS (HR 16.9; 95% CI 4.4-64.7) and OS (HR 5.3; 95% CI 1.2-22.2). In HPV-positive OPC, plasma HPV DNA correlated with worse RFS (p=0.02). Combined ctDNA and HPV DNA achieved 100% sensitivity and 73% specificity. CONCLUSIONS: ctDNA detection post-treatment predicts outcomes in LA-HNSCC. MERIDIAN provides preliminary evidence for MRD interception with rilvegostomig, showing durable ctDNA clearance.

Authors: Niida K, Yamamoto Y, Miyake T, Hayashi M, Tange K, Watanabe T, Yoshida O, Tokumoto Y, Tomida H, Takeshita E, et al.
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0363551
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43077432



Abstract:
Gut microbiota and periodontal diseases are potential risk factors for duodenal mucosa-associated microbiota in fibrosis progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease; however, the specific contribution of duodenal mucosa-associated microbiota remains unclear. Therefore, in this prospective study, we investigated its association with liver stiffness to elucidate its role in disease progression. Duodenal brush samples were collected during endoscopy from patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, classified by liver stiffness measurement into advanced (liver stiffness measurement>8.7 kPa, n = 10) and non-advanced (n = 20) groups. Extracted DNA was subjected to shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Analyses included taxonomy, diversity, differential abundance (edgeR), correlation (Spearman), and receiver operating characteristic predictive modeling, focusing on periodontal bacteria. While microbial diversity did not differ, advanced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease was characterized by the enrichment of the phylum Pseudomonadota and the genera Haemophilus and Klebsiella. Eight periodontal bacteria, including Campylobacter rectus, Porphyromonas gingivalis, and Fusobacterium nucleatum, were significantly enriched in patients with advanced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (P < 0.05) and correlated with liver fibrosis markers. A model based on these bacteria discriminated advanced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease with an AUC of 0.82 (95% CI, 0.634-1.000). Duodenal mucosa-associated microbiota alterations, particularly the enrichment of eight periodontal species, were associated with fibrosis severity. These findings highlight the role of the oral-gut-liver axis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease progression and suggest potential microbial biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

Authors: Endoh M, Tsuji Y, Jinushi T, Kurihara S, Higuchi T, Takayanagi A, Yamagishi A, Nomoto T
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0338683
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43077421



Abstract:
Manual toothbrushes are the most widely used for daily plaque control.　Although proper toothbrushing technique is crucial for effective plaque removal, improving and sustaining these skills remains challenging. Consequently, selecting an appropriate toothbrush is essential for maintaining optimal oral health. Despite various toothbrushes available, objective evaluation of the functional index of a toothbrush remains elusive. This study aimed to develop a comprehensive and objective evaluation method for toothbrush function using standardized models. For comprehensive evaluation, the assessed surface was divided into three elements (convex, concave, and flat). Two standardized evaluation models were developed: the smooth and interproximal surface model, which assesses the cleaning ability of both smooth and interproximal surfaces, and the single half cylinder model (SHC model), which measures the following ability of the toothbrush bristles on convex surfaces. Two types of test toothbrushes were used: small toothbrush with simple structure (toothbrush S) and large, functionally designed toothbrush (toothbrush G). Statistical analyses were performed using t‑tests and Bonferroni correction was applied when multiple comparisons were performed. The results indicated that toothbrush G had equal or greater cleaning ability than toothbrush S across all tested angles in the smooth and interproximal surface model. The minimum following load necessary for effective cleaning without bristle bounce was significantly lower (p = 0.01) for toothbrush G (1.25 N) than for toothbrush S (3.84 N), suggesting that toothbrush G is less dependent on brushing technique and more suitable for a wide range of individuals, regardless of their brushing skills. In this study, we confirmed that it is possible to significantly detect differences in toothbrush functionality (cleaning and following ability of toothbrush) by using two in vitro models of partial tooth-surface. Continued development of these models can potentially contribute to the standardization of toothbrush evaluation.

Authors: Schaefer J, Son L, Fang Z, Walvekar RR
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70562
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43076213



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stage at diagnosis is a strong predictor of survival in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC). Gulf South population-level data on these disparities remain limited. METHODS: We analyzed 1344 patients with known stage at diagnosis from Louisiana Tumor Registry data (n = 1698 cases, 2018-2023). Geographic access was operationalized as straight-line distance from parish centroid to the nearest academic medical center (AMC), categorized as < 25, 25-50, and > 50 miles. Multivariable logistic regression examined predictors of advanced-stage presentation (Stage III-IV) and nodal burden (N2-N3). RESULTS: Advanced-stage disease increased with distance from AMC (33.8%, 38.7%, 46.6%; Mantel-Haenszel χ2 = 13.4, p = 0.0003). Distance > 50 miles independently predicted advanced-stage presentation (OR 1.56, p = 0.008) and high nodal burden (OR 1.44, p = 0.030). Black race (OR 2.25), Medicaid (OR 1.62), and smoking (OR 2.91) were independent predictors. HPV-positive histology was strongly protective (OR 0.33, p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Distance from specialty care independently predicts advanced-stage OPSCC and extensive nodal disease even after controlling for HPV status, race, insurance, and socioeconomic factors, supporting targeted teleoncology expansion and rural outreach initiatives.

Authors: Hack S, Karni RJ, Coblens O, Hayu D, Sonnino R, Minkowitz G, Krinsky D, Locatello LG, Malkin BD, Rivero A, et al.
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70497
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43076196



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the quality of patient-facing thyroid cancer information generated by clinicians, large language models (LLMs), and web search results using parallel expert and layperson evaluation under blinded conditions. STUDY DESIGN: Blinded comparative evaluation study. SETTING: Online, text-based assessment of patient-facing health information. METHODS: Thirty commonly searched thyroid cancer questions were identified using Google Trends. For each question, patient-facing answers were generated by a fellowship-trained head and neck surgeon, 5 widely used LLMs (GPT-4, GPT-5, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek), and the first nonsponsored Google search result. Responses were anonymised and source-blinded. Seven attending physicians evaluated responses using the Quality Analysis of Medical AI (QAMAI) framework across 5 domains, and 15 lay participants evaluated the same responses across 4 patient-centred domains. Ratings were analysed at the question level using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), Friedman tests, Kendall's W, and post-hoc Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. RESULTS: Expert inter-rater reliability was good across domains (ICC 0.78-0.82). Expert ratings differed significantly across sources (P < .001; Kendall's W = 0.70-0.81), with Claude achieving the highest expert scores and Google-derived responses the lowest. Layperson ratings also differed significantly (P < .001; Kendall's W = 0.70-0.87) but clustered near the upper end of the scale, indicating a ceiling effect. The largest expert-rated differences occurred for treatment-related questions, particularly radioactive iodine therapy. CONCLUSION: Patient-facing thyroid cancer information quality varies across clinicians, LLMs, and web search results. Divergence between expert and layperson assessments indicates that perceived clarity and reassurance do not reliably reflect expert-defined completeness or clinical robustness.

Authors: Lin EY, Zhou AS, Grey S
Journal: The Annals of otology, rhinology, and laryngology | DOI: 10.1177/00034894261511058
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43075940



Abstract:
Nasal septal perforation (NSP) is a known complication of nasal trauma such as surgery or cauterization, intranasal drug use, autoinflammatory or autoimmune conditions, and infection. Cryoglobulinemic vasculitis (CV) is a less common cause of NSP in which immune complexes precipitate in and occlude small vessels, leading to ischemic necrosis of the nasal septal mucosa. This is a case report of a 75-year-old female patient with monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) and associated type I CV who presented with longstanding, recurrent bilateral nasal crusting, and was found to have a large anterior NSP with normal-appearing margins. Given her otherwise unremarkable medical or social history, her presentation was most likely attributable to the known CV. Biopsy to rule out malignancy was deferred, and it was anticipated that there would significant improvement in sinonasal symptoms with treatment of the underlying conditions. Therefore, the patient was initiated on low dose prednisone with subsequent taper, in addition to pre-existing plasma cell-directed therapy and dexamethasone, and the nasal crusting and drainage significantly improved after 2 weeks without need for surgical intervention.
